</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Sigma Analysis</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Further to the analysis done in the main paper above, we show how well <math id="A5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> correlates with different loss functions (<math id="A5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}+disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}+disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}}({\bm{x}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}}({\bm{x}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>) and the orderings that they induce. Our prediction <math id="A5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> most closely correlates with <math id="A5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}+disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}+disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> (the two orderings have a Kendall-Tau correlation of 0.67) which is unsurprising as it is trained to predict this loss. However, it still predicts both <math id="A5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}}({\bm{x}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}}({\bm{x}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> (Kendall-Tau correlation of 0.65) and <math id="A5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> (Kendall-Tau correlation of 0.63) well.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">When we train our uncertainty estimator to predict <math id="A5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}}({\bm{x}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}}({\bm{x}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>, the correlation with the ordering induced by <math id="A5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}}({\bm{x}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}}({\bm{x}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> (Kendall-Tau=0.73) increases but at the same time it correlates significantly less strongly with the order based on <math id="A5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> (Kendall-Tau=0.56).</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">When we train with <math id="A5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>, we still get a relative strong correlation with the ordering induced by <math id="A5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> (Kendall-Tau=0.62), but much less so with the <math id="A5.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}}({\bm{x}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}}({\bm{x}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> order (Kendall-Tau=0.34).</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F14" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_3">

</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 14: </span>
a, b, c) We show that the predicted <math id="A5.F14.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log\sigma_{i}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log\sigma_{i}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, the output of <math id="A5.F14.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi_{\vartheta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ψ</mi><mi>ϑ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi_{\vartheta}</annotation></semantics></math> on gallery images, and <math id="A5.F14.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}+disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}+disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.F14.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}}({\bm{x}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}}({\bm{x}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A5.F14.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log\mathcal{L}_{disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log\mathcal{L}_{disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively, are are well correlated.
c) We sort <math id="A5.F14.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\bm{x}}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\bm{x}}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> once by <math id="A5.F14.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{i}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{i}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and once by <math id="A5.F14.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}+disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}+disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.F14.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}}({\bm{x}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{l_{2}}({\bm{x}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A5.F14.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{disc}({\bm{x}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively, to get two sets of orderings. Here, for each <math id="A5.F14.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\bm{x}}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\bm{x}}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> we plot its order in the first ordering vs its order in the second ordering, and observe great correlation (Kendall-Tau correlation=0.67 (0.65, and 0.63 respectively)).</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Backfilling Order Analysis - VGGFace2-Gender</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We now analyse which types of classes are backfilled first using our FastFill method on the VGGFace2-Gender dataset. We group the classes into a minority (female) and majority group (male). As seen in Figure <a href="#A6.F15" title="Figure 15 ‣ Appendix F Backfilling Order Analysis - VGGFace2-Gender ‣ FastFill: Efficient Compatible Model Update" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a> FastFill prioritizes the minority class for early backfilling which explains the behaviour seen in <a href="#S5.SS3" title="5.3 Updating biased models ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ FastFill: Efficient Compatible Model Update" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.3</span></a> in the main paper.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F15" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="A6.F15.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2303.04766v1/plots/faces_gender_order_per_gender_bar_chart_FastFill.png" id="A6.F15.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:548/520;" width="548" height="520" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">(a) </span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="A6.F15.sf2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2303.04766v1/plots/faces_gender_order_per_gender_bar_chart_FCT.png" id="A6.F15.sf2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:548/520;" width="548" height="520" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">(b) </span></figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 15: </span>We compare the backfilling order of the minority (female) and majority (male) classes using (a) FastFill, and (b) FCT-Random. FastFill prioritizes the minority group and backfills the female gallery images first. As a results, FastFill achieves the new model accuracy gap after only <math id="A6.F15.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim 25\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim 25\%</annotation></semantics></math> of backfilling.</figcaption>
</figure>
